questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Your riding jacket should fit snugly but not restrict your movement. It should not flap in the wind.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will not help and is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should be your first concern when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection comes first. Choose a helmet that fastens securely, fits correctly, and meets DOT standards.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: Having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if you are below the legal blood alcohol limit.

questions.question: If hazards are to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives maximum protection when it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: A position that makes you visible and keeps a safe space around your motorcycle.
Any position you prefer, without thinking about other vehicles.
A position close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A position that makes you visible and keeps a safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. Good riders change their position as road conditions change.

questions.question: What does long-term wind noise do to your hearing?

options.text: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
It is just a normal part of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when you ride. It will protect you from wind noise while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light will turn red soon.
The traffic light will turn green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light will turn red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What should you do when borrowing a motorcycle?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as on your motorcycle.
Take it on the highway right away.
Get used to it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get used to it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a controlled area before riding on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, like farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely and go only when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose and flapping in the wind.
Snug so it does not flap in the wind.
Not made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they do not flap, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Limit how much you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how much you ride each day.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest even if you don't feel tired. Most experienced riders do not ride more than six hours per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tire faster. Dress properly to protect yourself from the elements.

questions.question: What happens when you lock your brakes?
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks when stopping on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What will you NOT be asked to identify during a pre-trip inspection on the motorcycle skills test?
questions.explanation: During your skills test, you will be asked to identify the starter, kill switch, clutch (if your motorcycle has one), throttle, gear selector, headlight dimmer switch, brakes, turn signals, and horn.

questions.question: What can happen if a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast?

options.text: They have better control of their motorcycle.
They experience a more stable ride.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to lose control. The motorcycle may drift into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear when riding. Good choices include long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, over-the-ankle closed-toe boots, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible to stay safe.

questions.question: How should you stop your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride in the left part of the lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Follow the vehicle in front closely to use their headlights.
Reduce your speed to better avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to better avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than you would during the day. This gives you a better chance to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: What type of shoes are best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection when riding. They should be tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: By law, what must motorcycle helmets meet?

options.text: Must be a dark color with no glare.

questions.explanation: Riders and passengers must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation safety standards. The helmet manufacturer must certify that it meets federal requirements.
